q.s: Kot Diji, a site with a pre-Harappan as well as a Harappan level, is located in:
q.x: Kot Diji lies in Sindh (Pakistan) and shows a pre-Harappan level below the Harappan one.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Harappan site?
q.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur) is known for a Mauryan copper-plate inscription; Surkotada and Desalpur are Harappan sites in Kachchh.

q.s: Which Harappan site has yielded 56 skeletons from its Mound 7, including that of a woman about 4,600 years old?
q.x: Rakhigarhi (Haryana) Mound 7 is a cemetery that yielded 56 skeletons.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The huddled skeletons at Mohenjodaro are now read as evidence of a massacre.
Kalibangan has yielded circular pits with grave goods but no skeleton.
Kalibangan has yielded only one type of burial.
Rakhigarhi's Mound 7 has yielded no skeletons.
q.x: Kalibangan has three burial types; the Mohenjodaro skeletons are now read as multiple burials.

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most reliable source for ancient Indian history?
q.x: Inscriptions are contemporary, datable and hard to alter, so they are the most reliable source.

q.s: The earliest land-grant records in India belong to the:
q.x: The earliest land grants in India are Satavahana records.

q.s: Who deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837?
q.x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837; Turnour identified 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' with Ashoka.

q.s: Ashoka's Kandahar bilingual inscription is written in:
q.x: The Kandahar bilingual is in Greek and Aramaic, not Kharosthi.

q.s: Who wrote 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'?
q.x: Tilak placed the Aryan home in the Arctic; Dayananda (Satyarth Prakash) held the Tibet view.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Dayananda Saraswati wrote The Arctic Home in the Vedas.
Ganganath Jha placed the original home of the Aryans in Central Asia.
A.C. Das placed the original home of the Aryans in Sapta Sindhu.
The Tibet theory is the mainstream view today.
q.x: Tilak wrote the Arctic Home; Jha favoured Brahmarshi Desha; the mainstream view is the Eurasian steppe.

q.s: Kumarila Bhatta, who defended Vedic ritual against Buddhism, was an exponent of which school?
q.x: Purva (Karma) Mimamsa centres on Vedic ritual action; Kumarila was its leading exponent.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy?
q.x: Charvaka (Lokayata) is a heterodox materialist school.

q.s: Ashoka's inscription at Rummindei (Lumbini) in Nepal is a:
q.x: The Rummindei pillar marks the Buddha's birthplace and records the reduction of tax at Lumbini.

q.s: The name 'Ashoka' (not just 'Devanampiya Piyadasi') first appeared in which inscription?
q.x: The Maski minor rock edict (Raichur, Karnataka) was the first found to name Ashoka.

q.s: The Maitrakas, a successor power of the Guptas, ruled from:
q.x: Maitrakas - Valabhi (Gujarat); Pushyabhutis - Thanesar; Maukharis - Kannauj; Aulikaras - Mandsaur.

q.s: Which of the following successor powers of the Guptas is NOT correctly matched with its seat?
q.x: The Maitrakas ruled from Valabhi; the Maukharis held Kannauj.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Yashodharman is correct?
o: He was a Maukhari king of Kannauj.
He was an Aulikara king of Malwa.
He was defeated by the Huna king Mihirakula.
q.x: Yashodharman of Mandsaur defeated Mihirakula c. 528 CE and his rise weakened the Guptas.

q.s: Yashodharman's victory pillars are found at:
q.x: The Sondani (Mandsaur) pillars, c. 532 CE, record his victories, including over Mihirakula.

q.s: Which of the following work - author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Kamasutra is by Vatsyayana; Kamandaka wrote the Nitisara.

q.s: The Hitopadesha is based on the:
q.x: Narayana's Hitopadesha retells the fables of the Panchatantra.

q.s: Banabhatta adorned the court of:
q.x: Bana wrote the Harshacharita and Kadambari at Harsha's court.

q.s: Bhavabhuti, author of Uttararamacharita, was the court poet of:
q.x: Bhavabhuti was at Yashovarman's court; Harisena was at Samudragupta's and Kalidasa at Chandragupta II's.

q.s: Which of the following Chola village committees is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Pon variyam dealt with gold, finance and currency.

q.s: Which inscriptions give a detailed account of the election of Chola village committees?
q.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I describe the kudavolai election to the sabha's committees.

q.s: The Mongol leader Qutlugh Khwaja was defeated at Kili (1299) during the reign of:
q.x: Alauddin faced repeated Mongol attacks: Kili 1299, Delhi 1303 (Targhi), Amroha 1305, Ravi 1306.

q.s: Who set up the Diwan-i-Arz (military department) in the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: Balban created the Diwan-i-Arz under the Ariz-i-Mumalik; Alauddin expanded the standing army.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the army of the Delhi Sultanate is correct?
o: Cavalry horses were mainly imported from Bengal.
War elephants were a monopoly of the Sultan.
The Diwan-i-Arz was set up by Alauddin Khalji.
War elephants were kept mainly by the iqtadars.
q.x: Elephants were the Sultan's monopoly; horses came mainly from Central Asia and Arabia.

q.s: Zakat, a tax of the Delhi Sultanate, was charged at about:
q.x: Zakat was about 2.5% of wealth, paid by Muslims; khams was the share of booty.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a sharia tax of the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: Ghari (house tax) and charai (grazing tax) were non-sharia taxes; zakat, jizya, kharaj and khams were sharia taxes.

q.s: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Sufi saint?
q.x: Khusrau was a devoted disciple of the Chishti saint Nizamuddin Auliya.

q.s: The Baburnama was translated into Persian in 1589 by:
q.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan made the Persian translation for Akbar.

q.s: Babur's memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, was originally written in:
q.x: It was written in Chaghatai Turki; Beveridge translated it into English from the Turki.

q.s: Who defended the Golconda fort against Aurangzeb in 1687?
q.x: Abdur Razzaq Lari held the fort; the traitor Abdullah Pani opened a gate.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal conquest of Golconda (1687) is correct?
o: Abul Hasan Tana Shah was buried at Khuldabad.
Mir Jumla defended the Golconda fort.
Tana Shah was exiled to Gwalior.
Bhakta Ramadasu was the son of Madanna.
q.x: Tana Shah was imprisoned at Daulatabad and buried at Khuldabad; Ramadasu was Madanna's nephew.

q.s: Under the Mughals, a mansabdar who received his salary in cash was called:
q.x: A mansabdar was paid either in cash (naqdi) or by a revenue assignment (jagir); neither was hereditary.

q.s: Guru Ravidas envisioned an ideal city without sorrow, which he called:
q.x: Ravidas, of a leather-tanner background, dreamt of Begampura; 41 of his shabdas are in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT written by Jnaneshwar?
q.x: The Dasbodh is by Ramdas; the Jnaneshwari is also called the Bhavartha Dipika.

q.s: Pandharpur, the seat of the Varkari sect, stands on the bank of the:
q.x: Pandharpur (Vithoba temple) lies on the Chandrabhaga, as the Bhima is called there.

q.s: The Kowthalam dargah, where the Ugadi Panchanga Shravanam is read jointly by a Sufi and a Brahmin priest, is in:
q.x: Kowthalam is in Kurnool district, an example of Sufi-Bhakti syncretism in Andhra.

q.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda was a disciple of the Sufi saint:
q.x: Tana Shah was a disciple of Shah Raju Qattal of Hyderabad.

q.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler allowed Albuquerque to build a fort at Bhatkal for the horse trade?
q.x: Krishnadeva Raya wanted Arab and Persian horses, so he allowed the Bhatkal fort.

q.s: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 from the:
q.x: Goa was taken from Bijapur, with help from the Vijayanagara naval chief Timmaju.

q.s: Which was the earliest of the following French settlements, founded in 1669?
q.x: Masulipatnam 1669, Pondicherry 1674, Mahe 1725, Karaikal 1739.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a French settlement in India?
q.x: Tranquebar was a Danish settlement.

q.s: Tantia Tope was betrayed to the British by:
q.x: Man Singh, Raja of Narwar, betrayed Tantia Tope in 1859.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Jhansi lapsed to the British in 1848.
Jhansi was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1854.
The sons of Bahadur Shah II were shot by John Nicholson.
Rani Lakshmibai died fighting Colin Campbell.
q.x: Jhansi lapsed in 1854; Hodson shot the princes; the Rani fell fighting Hugh Rose.

q.s: The First Carnatic War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended it and Madras was restored to the English.

q.s: In the First Carnatic War, the French defeated the army of Nawab Anwaruddin at:
q.x: At St. Thome (Adyar) a small French force routed the Nawab's large army.

q.s: Siraj-ud-Daulah killed his rival Shaukat Jang, Nawab of Purnea, at the battle of:
q.x: Shaukat Jang fell at Manihari (1756); Alivardi had killed Sarfaraz Khan at Giria.

q.s: Who succeeded Mir Jafar as Nawab of Bengal in 1765?
q.x: Mir Jafar died in 1765 and his son Najm-ud-daula became Nawab.

q.s: The battle of Chinsura (Bidara) of 1759 was fought between the English and the:
q.x: Mir Jafar's intrigue with the Dutch led to their defeat at Bidara (Chinsura) in 1759.

q.s: At the battle of Porto Novo (1781), Haidar Ali was defeated by:
q.x: Eyre Coote's victory at Porto Novo saved Madras after Pollilur.

q.s: In which battle of 1780 did Haidar Ali and Tipu destroy Col. William Baillie's force?
q.x: Pollilur (10 September 1780) was one of the worst British defeats in India.

q.s: The Third Anglo-Mysore War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: By the Treaty of Srirangapatnam Tipu gave up Malabar, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal.

q.s: The Ryotwari system was first introduced in the Bara Mahal by:
q.x: Read and Munro began the Ryotwari system in the Bara Mahal after 1792.

q.s: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784), which ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War, was concluded by the English with:
q.x: Haidar Ali died in December 1782, so the treaty was made with Tipu.

q.s: The First Anglo-Mysore War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Madras (April 1769) provided for mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.

q.s: The annexation of Sindh (1843), called the 'Tail of the Afghan Storm', took place under Governor-General:
q.x: Charles Napier conquered Sindh in 1843 under Ellenborough, to restore prestige lost in the First Afghan War.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT annexed by Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse?
q.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance.

q.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War was ended by the Treaty of:
q.x: By the Treaty of Salbai the English kept Salsette and Sindhia stood guarantor for peace.

q.s: Which of the following treaties is NOT related to the Anglo-Maratha wars?
q.x: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Northern Circars ceded to the English in 1766?
q.x: The 1766 Circars were Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore and Mustafanagar (Kondapalli); Guntur was kept as Basalat Jang's estate.

q.s: Guntur, the fifth Northern Circar, was held in 1766 as the estate (jagir) of:
q.x: Guntur (Murtazanagar) was Basalat Jang's estate and passed to the English later (1788).

q.s: Who among the following was the earliest to serve as Governor-General?
q.x: Wellesley (1798-1805), Minto I (1807-13), Amherst (1823-28), Auckland (1836-42).

q.s: The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26) took place during the tenure of:
q.x: Amherst's tenure saw the First Burmese War, ended by the Treaty of Yandabo.

q.s: The first Famine Commission (1880), headed by Richard Strachey, was set up under Viceroy:
q.x: Strachey Commission under Lytton; Lyall under Elgin II; MacDonnell under Curzon.

q.s: The MacDonnell Famine Commission (1901) was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Curzon appointed the MacDonnell Commission after the famine of 1899-1900.

q.s: Thomas Munro served as the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts, with headquarters at:
q.x: Munro was Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts (1800-07) from Anantapur.

q.s: Which of the following posts was NOT held by Thomas Munro?
o: Assistant to Read in the Baramahal
q.x: Munro was Governor of Madras (1820-27) but never Governor-General.

q.s: Which nationalist linked colonial famines with high land revenue and the drain of wealth in his 'Economic History of India'?
q.x: R.C. Dutt (with Dadabhai Naoroji) traced famines to rigid land revenue, food exports and the drain.

q.s: Which of the following newspaper - person pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Al-Hilal was Abul Kalam Azad's paper; Mohammad Ali ran Comrade; Bande Mataram was a Calcutta paper of Aurobindo and B.C. Pal.

q.s: The Rowlatt Act was popularly described as:
o: No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel
q.x: It allowed detention without trial and without appeal, hence the slogan.

q.s: Gandhi called the nationwide hartal of the Rowlatt Satyagraha on:
q.x: The hartal was on 6 April 1919; Jallianwala Bagh was on 13 April; the satyagraha was suspended on 18 April.

q.s: Who was the first in Andhra to start a night school and promote co-education?
q.x: Veeresalingam also fought dowry, the nautch and corruption mainly through the press.

q.s: Barnaparichay, a Bengali alphabet primer, was written by:
q.x: Vidyasagar wrote Barnaparichay and opened the Sanskrit College to non-Brahmins.

q.s: The Bethune School for girls in Calcutta was founded in 1849 by:
q.x: J.E.D. Bethune founded it; Vidyasagar became its secretary in 1850.

q.s: Gandhi took the term 'Harijan' (children of God) from the Gujarati saint:
q.x: Narsi Mehta used the word; Ambedkar rejected it.

q.s: The first issue of Gandhi's weekly 'Harijan' came out in February 1933 from:
q.x: Harijan began at Poona on 11 February 1933.

q.s: Ambedkar's Navayana Buddhism rejects which of the following?
q.x: Navayana rejects karma, rebirth and monasticism and stresses social equality.

q.s: Buddhists were brought under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 in the year:
q.x: Sikhs were included in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990.

q.s: The Dev Samaj was founded at:
q.x: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj at Lahore (1887); the Prarthana Samaj was at Bombay.

q.s: Which of the following reform bodies is NOT correctly matched with its centre?
q.x: The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay (1867).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a pre-Congress political association?
q.x: The Servants of India Society was founded by Gokhale in 1905; the others date from 1852-1876.

q.s: The East India Association was founded in London in 1866 by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji set it up to influence British opinion; Banerjea founded the Indian Association.

q.s: Who propounded the 'drain of wealth' theory?
q.x: Naoroji set it out in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'; Sir Syed rejected it, seeing British rule as modernising.

q.s: Who was the first principal of the Bengal National College?
q.x: Aurobindo headed the college set up under the National Council of Education (1906).

q.s: The National Council of Education set up in 1906 later grew into:
q.x: The NCE (15 August 1906) evolved into Jadavpur University.

q.s: The Congress split between Moderates and Extremists took place at the session of:
q.x: At Surat the Extremists wanted Tilak or Lajpat Rai as president; the Moderates kept the Congress machinery.

q.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT a Moderate at the time of the Surat split?
q.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was an Extremist; Rash Behari Ghosh presided over the Surat session.

q.s: Madan Lal Dhingra shot Sir William Curzon Wyllie in London in:
q.x: Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie on 1 July 1909 and was hanged at Pentonville in August 1909.

q.s: Annie Besant's Home Rule League (1916) had its headquarters at:
q.x: Tilak's league was launched at Belgaum; Besant's worked from Adyar and had about 200 branches.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an area of Tilak's Home Rule League?
q.x: Tilak's league covered Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, CP and Berar; Besant's covered the rest of India.

q.s: 'Veera Telangana – Naa Anubhavalu, Gnapakalu' was written by:
q.x: It is Ravi Narayana Reddy's memoir; Mallu Swarajyam was a woman fighter of the struggle.

q.s: In Champaran, the 'tinkathia' system obliged tenants to grow indigo on:
q.x: Tinkathia meant indigo on 3 kathas per bigha (3/20th); sharahbeshi was enhanced rent.

q.s: The Bengal Indigo Revolt took place in:
q.x: After the 1859-60 revolt indigo planting shifted to Bihar.

q.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Vedaranyam on the Tanjore coast?
q.x: Rajaji marched from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam; Kelappan led it in Malabar.

q.s: Which of the following region - Salt Satyagraha leader pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Gopabandhu Choudhury led the satyagraha in Orissa.

q.s: The first INA trial (1945) of Shah Nawaz Khan, P.K. Sahgal and G.S. Dhillon was held at:
q.x: The Red Fort trial ended with Auchinleck remitting the sentences in January 1946.

q.s: The Royal Indian Navy revolt broke out in Bombay in:
q.x: The RIN ratings revolted on 18 February 1946.

q.s: The C.R. Formula, which proposed a plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas after the war, was put forward in:
q.x: Rajagopalachari's formula came in March 1944; the Desai-Liaquat Pact followed in January 1945.

q.s: Konda Venkatappayya was a co-founder and first editor of:
q.x: He founded Krishna Patrika in 1902 with Dasu Narayana Rao; Andhra Patrika was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's.

q.s: The first Andhra Mahasabha was held in 1913 at:
q.x: The first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla, with Konda Venkatappayya as secretary.

q.s: Gandhi described which of the following as the last and most potent weapon of satyagraha?
q.x: In Harijan (1946) he called fasting unto death the last resort, after all other avenues failed.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a method of Gandhian satyagraha?
q.x: Satyagraha rests on non-violence.

q.s: The 'Andhra Circular' of the Quit India Movement came to be known as the:
q.x: The police seized a copy at the Kurnool Congress office; it was issued by the APCC, not the Working Committee.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Andhra Circular of 1942 is correct?
o: It was issued by the Congress Working Committee.
It was dated after the AICC session of 8 August 1942.
It was issued by the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee.
The related APCC meeting was presided over by Tanguturi Prakasam.
q.x: Dated 29 July 1942, it was an APCC circular; Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the meeting.

q.s: Who presided over the Belgaum session of the Congress (1924)?
q.x: Belgaum 1924 was Gandhi's only Congress presidency.

q.s: Who was the first Indian woman to be President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur (1925); Annie Besant (Calcutta 1917) was the first woman president.

q.s: Who was called the 'Socrates of Maharashtra'?
q.x: Gokhale bore the title; Tilak was 'Lokmanya'.

q.s: The Nair Service Society was founded by:
q.x: Mannathu Padmanabhan ('Bharatha Kesari') founded the NSS; Kelappan led the Guruvayur satyagraha.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee is correct?
o: It was chaired by Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
It was set up in 1972 to fix land ceilings.
It was set up in 2004 and made 104 recommendations on land issues.
q.x: Chaired by minister Koneru Ranga Rao, it reviewed land distribution to the poor.

q.s: Who moved the resolution for linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918?
q.x: B.N. Sarma moved it; Surendranath Banerjee said 'the time has not come'.

q.s: The Madras Partition Committee (1949), which dealt with dividing assets between Madras and Andhra, was headed by:
q.x: Chief Minister Kumaraswamy Raja headed it; Prakasam gave a separate note.

q.s: The Dhar Commission (1948) on linguistic provinces was appointed by the:
q.x: Rajendra Prasad, as President of the Constituent Assembly, appointed it; it rejected language as the main basis.

q.s: Which of the following committees, after the Dhar Commission, also examined the linguistic provinces question in 1948-49?
q.x: The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi) followed the Dhar Commission; Fazl Ali came in 1953.

q.s: Who coined the word 'Visalandhra' and wrote 'Visalandhralo Prajarajyam'?
q.x: Sundarayya, later first General Secretary of the CPI(M) (1964), wrote it.

q.s: How many Telugu districts of Hyderabad State were merged with Andhra State to form Andhra Pradesh in 1956?
q.x: Nine Telangana districts joined the eleven districts of Andhra State on 1 November 1956.

q.s: The name 'Andhra Pradesh' for the new State in 1956 was chosen by the:
q.x: The draft Bill said 'Andhra Telangana'; the Joint Select Committee chose 'Andhra Pradesh'.

q.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Telangana Regional Committee?
q.x: K. Achyuta Reddy, MLA from Kodangal, was its first Chairman.

q.s: The Telangana Regional Committee was constituted under which provision?
q.x: It rested on Article 371(1) and the 1958 Order; Article 371D came with the 32nd Amendment (1973).

q.s: Which of the following States was NOT formed in the year 2000?
q.x: Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand were formed in November 2000; Telangana on 2 June 2014.

q.s: Which of the following States was formed on 1 November 2000?
q.x: Chhattisgarh 1 Nov, Uttarakhand 9 Nov, Jharkhand 15 Nov 2000.

q.s: The Kondamudi copper plates are the only record of which dynasty?
q.x: They were issued by Jayavarma of the Brihatphalayana family, ruling from Koduru.

q.s: The title 'Ekabrahmana' was assumed by:
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni called himself Ekabrahmana and Varnasankarya-nirodhaka (Nasik prasasti).

q.s: Which Satavahana ruler bore the title 'Dakshinapatheshwara'?
q.x: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi was Dakshinapatheshwara; Satakarni I was Dakshinapathapati.

q.s: Which place is regarded by Barnett, V.A. Smith and Burgess as the first capital of the Satavahanas?
q.x: Srikakulam in Krishna district; Kotilingala (Karimnagar) is another claimed early centre.

q.s: Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) was the capital of the:
q.x: Vijayapuri was the Ikshvaku capital.

q.s: In the Satavahana period, 'vetti' meant:
q.x: Vetti was forced labour; karukara taxed artisans and sulka was the water tax.

q.s: Which of the following Satavahana terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sulka was the water tax; vetti was forced labour.

q.s: Which of the following statements about guild banking in the Satavahana period is correct?
o: Ushavadatta deposited 2,000 karshapanas with a weavers' guild at Govardhana.
Guilds lent money at 12% a month.
Ushavadatta was the son of Nahapana.
q.x: The rate was about 12% a year; Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law.

q.s: Thotlakonda, a Buddhist site near Visakhapatnam, was first spotted in an aerial survey by the:
q.x: An Indian Navy aerial survey revealed it; excavations (1988-92) found Satavahana and Roman coins.

q.s: A pot of 3,730 lead coins of the Satavahana period was found in 2024 at:
q.x: The 2024 hoard came from Phanigiri (Suryapet district).

q.s: The Gathasaptasati of Hala was composed in:
q.x: Hala's anthology is in Prakrit and is the main literary source on Satavahana society.

q.s: Besides Buddhism, which of the following did NOT flourish under the Ikshvakus?
q.x: Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship flourished alongside Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda; Islam came many centuries later.

q.s: The early Vishnukundin capital Indrapalanagara has been identified with:
q.x: Indrapalanagara (Tummalagudem, Nalgonda) was built by Indravarma; Amarapura is Munnanuru.

q.s: The founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, Dantidurga, overthrew the Badami Chalukya ruler:
q.x: Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II; his inscription is in the Dashavatara cave (Cave 15) at Ellora.

q.s: The Rashtrakuta capital Manyakheta was built by:
q.x: Amoghavarsha I, author of Kavirajamarga, built Manyakheta.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Eastern Chalukya grants to the Jains is correct?
o: Queen Ayyana Mahadevi won the Kaluchumbarru grant.
Gunaga Vijayaditya issued the Maliyapundi grant.
Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda to the Jains.
The Eastern Chalukyas made no grants to the Jains.
q.x: The courtesan Chamekamba won the Kaluchumbarru grant; Ammaraja II issued the Maliyapundi grant.

q.s: Which was the first Indian language to be declared a classical language (2004)?
q.x: Tamil got classical status in 2004; Telugu and Kannada in 2008.

q.s: The Tamil Ramayana, the Ramavataram, was written by:
q.x: Kamban wrote the Ramavataram; Tayumanavar was a Saiva saint-poet.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya won the Battle of Raichur in the year:
q.x: Raichur was won in 1520; Gulbarga was taken in 1523.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya took the title 'Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya' after restoring which Bahmani Sultan?
q.x: He freed and restored the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah.

q.s: The Amuktamalyada of Krishnadevaraya is valued as a source on statecraft because of its section on:
q.x: Its rajaniti section gives the king's advice on governance.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Veerashaivism?
o: Acceptance of the authority of the Vedas
q.x: Veerashaivism rejected the Vedas as well as caste, child marriage and sacrifice.

q.s: Who spread Veerashaivism in Andhra during the Kakatiya period?
q.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam in Telugu.

q.s: The temple at Arasavalli in Srikakulam district is dedicated to:
q.x: Arasavalli - Surya; Srikurmam - Kurma; Simhachalam - Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha.

q.s: Which of the following temple - deity pairs of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Mukhalingam's deity is Madhukeswara (Shiva).

q.s: Vijayanagara temples were built largely of:
q.x: The Deccan plateau gave easy access to local granite.

q.s: Which famine prompted Arthur Cotton's Dowleswaram anicut across the Godavari?
q.x: The Guntur (Nandana) famine was the trigger; the anicut was sanctioned in 1846.

q.s: The Dowleswaram anicut was built across the river:
q.x: Cotton's anicut at Dowleswaram is on the Godavari near Rajahmundry.

q.s: By 1917, how many Home Rule League branches were there in Andhra?
q.x: Andhra had 52 branches; Besant toured Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru after Lucknow 1916.

q.s: The 1944 session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha that brought it under communist control was held at:
q.x: After the Bhuvanagiri (Bhongir) session, a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha broke away.

q.s: Which journal was started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874 as his first journal?
q.x: Vivekavardhani (1874) was his first; Hasyasanjivani 1876, Sati Hitabodhini 1883.

q.s: Which of the following journals was NOT started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
q.x: Andhra Patrika was started by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

q.s: Atla Taddi, a festival of the women of Andhra, falls in the month of:
q.x: Atla Taddi is observed in Aswayuja; Kolla Pandalu (cockfights) belong to Sankranti.

q.s: Which Reddi king styled himself 'Karpura Vasantarayalu' and celebrated the Vasantotsavam?
q.x: Kumaragiri Reddy; Avachi Tippayashetti supplied the camphor and perfumes for the festival.

q.s: Which of the following food items of Andhra Pradesh received its GI tag in 2009?
q.x: Tirupati Laddu got its GI in 2009; Bandar Laddu in 2017; Tapeswaram Kaja has none.

q.s: Budithi bell and brass craft, a GI product of Andhra Pradesh, belongs to which district?
q.x: Budithi village is in Srikakulam district.

q.s: Who wrote the Telugu poem 'Firdausi'?
q.x: Jashuva's Firdausi tells of the Persian poet cheated of his reward by Sultan Mahmud.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Gurram Jashuva's poem 'Firdausi' is correct?
o: It was written by Sri Sri.
It presents the poet as a contented court flatterer.
It is about a poet generously rewarded by Sultan Mahmud.
It presents the poet as a rebel against royal patronage.
q.x: The poem is about Firdausi being cheated of his promised reward.

q.s: The rise of Dalit Mahasabhas and Dalit writing in Andhra followed which incident of 1985?
q.x: After Karamchedu (1985) came Dalit Mahasabhas and anthologies like Chikkanavutunna Pata (1995).

q.s: The Dalit poetry anthology 'Padunekkina Pata' (1996) was edited by:
q.x: G. Lakshmi Narasaiah edited Padunekkina Pata.

q.s: India and Jordan signed a twinning agreement between the Ellora caves and:
q.x: Petra (Jordan) and Ellora (India), both UNESCO sites, were twinned.

q.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king:
q.x: Krishna I built the rock-cut Kailasanatha temple (Cave 16).

q.s: The concept of 'culture circles' (Kulturkreis) belongs to which school of diffusionism?
q.x: Graebner and Schmidt - culture circles; Elliot Smith and Perry - Egypt as the source; Wissler - culture areas.

q.s: Who is associated with the technological theory of social change?
q.x: Veblen saw technology as the main driver of social change.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of achieved status?
q.x: Achieved statuses are earned; sex, age, caste, race and kinship are ascribed at birth.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an ascribed status?
q.x: Doctor is an achieved status.

q.s: Who was the first chairperson of the Central Social Welfare Board (1953)?
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh headed the CSWB from 1953.

q.s: The All India Women's Conference (1927) was founded by:
q.x: Margaret Cousins founded the AIWC; she and Besant also founded the Women's Indian Association (1917).

q.s: Who stood for the 'annihilation of caste' rather than its reform from within Hindu society?
q.x: Ambedkar sought legal-constitutional rights and the annihilation of caste; reform from within was Gandhi's approach.

q.s: The Siddhantam movement of 1933 in Andhra was related to:
q.x: Siddhantam was one of the earliest temple entry movements in Andhra.

q.s: The 112 Aspirational Districts are monitored by:
q.x: NITI Aayog runs the Aspirational Districts Programme.

q.s: Under the Rayalaseema industrial plan, the JSW steel plant is located in:
q.x: The JSW steel plant is in Kadapa; Royal Enfield is linked with Tirupati.

q.s: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, a protection order is given under:
q.x: s.17 right to reside; s.18 protection order; s.19 residence order; s.20 monetary relief.

q.s: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 has now been merged into the:
q.x: The 2008 Act was subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.

q.s: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation was set up under the:
q.x: ESIC dates from the ESI Act, 1948; the 2008 Act set up the National Social Security Board.

q.s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched on 23 September 2018 at:
q.x: PM-JAY was launched at Ranchi; it subsumed RSBY.

q.s: Which body implements Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at the national level?
q.x: The NHA implements it; State Health Agencies do so in States.

q.s: Which scheme for a slum-free India was subsumed into PMAY-Urban in 2015?
q.x: Rajiv Awas Yojana was merged into PMAY-U; Indira Awaas Yojana became PMAY-Gramin.

q.s: PMAY-Urban 2.0 (2024) targets the construction of how many urban houses?
q.x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore urban houses.

q.s: Which is the nodal agency for NTR Bharosa pensions in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: SERP (Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty) runs the doorstep pension delivery.

q.s: From 2024, the monthly old-age pension under NTR Bharosa in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: The pension was raised from Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000 under the renamed NTR Bharosa.

q.s: Which case held that the State cannot impose a reservation quota on unaided minority and non-minority institutions?
q.x: P.A. Inamdar barred State quotas in unaided institutions.

q.s: Article 30 of the Constitution gives minorities the right to:
q.x: Article 30 lets religious and linguistic minorities establish and administer educational institutions.

q.s: Article 370 was abrogated on:
q.x: On 5 August 2019 J&K's special status ended; the Supreme Court upheld this in December 2023.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 370 is correct?
o: The Supreme Court struck down its abrogation in 2023.
The Supreme Court upheld its abrogation in December 2023.
After abrogation, Ladakh became part of the UT of J&K.
q.x: The Court upheld the abrogation; J&K and Ladakh became separate Union Territories.

q.s: The India-Russia Declaration on Strategic Partnership was signed in:
q.x: It was signed in October 2000, so 2025 marked 25 years.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the I2U2 grouping?
q.x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the USA.

q.s: Which is India's oldest paramilitary force, raised in 1835?
q.x: The Assam Rifles was raised in 1835 as the Cachar Levy.

q.s: The Department of Border Management functions under the:
q.x: Created in 2004, it is part of the MHA.

q.s: The attack on the Indian Parliament took place on:
q.x: Parliament was attacked on 13 December 2001.

q.s: Which of the following attack - year pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Uri attack was in 2016; Pulwama was in 2019.

q.s: Who wrote 'The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation' (1966)?
q.x: Granville Austin wrote it; Wheare wrote 'Modern Constitutions'.

q.s: 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' was written by:
q.x: A.V. Dicey wrote it and set out the rule of law.

q.s: Which of the following provisions of the Constitution did NOT come into force on 26 November 1949?
q.x: Citizenship, elections, the provisional Parliament and transitional provisions took effect on 26 November 1949; the rest, including emergency provisions, on 26 January 1950.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise the 'living will' (advance directive) and dying with dignity under Article 21?
q.x: Common Cause (2018) upheld the living will; Aruna Shanbaug (2011) allowed passive euthanasia under High Court supervision.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Aruna Shanbaug (2011) upheld the living will.
Common Cause (2018) held that dying with dignity is not part of Article 21.
In Aruna Shanbaug (2011), passive euthanasia under High Court supervision was allowed.
q.x: The living will came in Common Cause (2018); Gian Kaur held that the right to life does not include the right to die.

q.s: The right of voters to know the details of candidates has been recognised as part of:
q.x: Candidate details, NOTA and ballot secrecy are read into Article 19(1)(a), though voting is a statutory right.

q.s: In Navtej Singh Johar (2018), the Supreme Court read down which provision?
q.x: It decriminalised consensual adult same-sex acts under Section 377 IPC; Section 497 (adultery) went in Joseph Shine.

q.s: The Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) was repealed in:
q.x: MISA was enacted in 1971 and repealed in 1977 by the Janata government.

q.s: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act was enacted in:
q.x: The 2013 Act bans sewer cleaning without protective gear.

q.s: Which of the following can be amended only by a special majority of Parliament along with ratification by half the States?
q.x: Election of the President (Art. 54-55) needs State ratification; DPSPs and FRs need only a special majority; Councils are created by simple majority.

q.s: A Legislative Council in a State is created or abolished by:
o: An Act of Parliament by simple majority
A constitutional amendment with State ratification
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: Under Article 169, Parliament acts by simple majority after the State Assembly's resolution.

q.s: Nagaland got statehood and Article 371A by the:
q.x: 13th - Nagaland; 53rd - Mizoram; 55th - Arunachal Pradesh; 56th - Goa.

q.s: Which of the following Article - State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Article 371A is for Nagaland; 371G Mizoram, 371H Arunachal Pradesh, 371I Goa.

q.s: The First Amendment (1951), which added the Ninth Schedule, was upheld by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Shankari Prasad upheld Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.

q.s: Article 15(4) was added by the First Amendment in response to the judgment in:
q.x: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) led to Article 15(4); Articles 31A-31B protected zamindari abolition laws.

q.s: Which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards?
q.x: Sec. 85 - KRMB and GRMB; Sec. 8 - Governor's responsibility in the common capital; Sec. 46(3) - backward-area package.

q.s: Section 8 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 gives the Governor special responsibility for:
o: Security of residents of the common capital
q.x: Sec. 8 concerns law and order and security in the common capital, Hyderabad.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Speaker's decision on defection is subject to judicial review?
q.x: Kihoto Hollohan upheld the Tenth Schedule but made the presiding officer's decision reviewable.

q.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, a member's vote against the party whip can be condoned within 15 days by:
q.x: Condonation is by the party, not by the presiding officer.

q.s: Under Article 102, unsoundness of mind disqualifies a member of Parliament only when:
o: It is declared by a competent court
q.x: Disqualification needs a declaration by a competent court; Parliament can exempt offices from 'office of profit' by law.

q.s: Which of the following statements about disqualification under Article 102 is correct?
o: 'Office of profit' is defined in the RP Act, 1951.
Unsoundness of mind disqualifies without any court declaration.
'Office of profit' is defined in Article 102.
Parliament may by law exempt an office from the office-of-profit disqualification.
q.x: 'Office of profit' is defined neither in the Constitution nor in the RP Act.

q.s: The 106th Constitutional Amendment (2023) reserves one-third of seats for women in which of the following?
o: Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
q.x: The Rajya Sabha and Councils are not covered; the Delhi Assembly is.

q.s: The women's reservation under the 106th Amendment will take effect after:
q.x: It begins after the first Census and delimitation following the Act and runs for 15 years, extendable by Parliament.

q.s: The Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha is:
q.x: The President appoints a senior member as Pro-Tem Speaker to swear in members and conduct the Speaker's election.

q.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
q.x: Meira Kumar became Speaker in 2009; Sumitra Mahajan was the second.

q.s: Which Lok Sabha Speaker later became President of India?
q.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy was Speaker (1967, 1977) and President (1977-82).

q.s: Who was the last Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha (2014-19)?
q.x: M. Thambidurai; the post has been vacant since June 2019 although Article 93 says the House 'shall' choose one.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: He has no casting vote while a resolution for his own removal is under consideration.
Filling the post is optional under the Constitution.
He is appointed by the President.
He cannot vote even when not in the Chair.
q.x: Article 93 says the House 'shall' choose a Deputy Speaker; when not in the Chair he votes like a member.

q.s: Which parliamentary committee is called the 'Ombudsman' of Parliament on citizens' grievances?
q.x: The Committee on Petitions examines citizens' representations.

q.s: Which of the following parliamentary committees is NOT correctly matched with its function?
o: Committee on Government Assurances - Ministers' promises
Business Advisory Committee - Ombudsman of Parliament
Committee on Subordinate Legislation - Delegated legislation
q.x: The Business Advisory Committee allots time for business.

q.s: In the 2024 Andhra Pradesh Assembly election, how many of the 175 seats did the NDA win?
q.x: The NDA won 164: TDP 135, Jana Sena 21, BJP 8; the YSRCP won 11.

q.s: Which party leads the NDA coalition government formed in Andhra Pradesh in 2024?
q.x: The TDP is the dominant partner, with the Jana Sena and the BJP as allies.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the President exercises the pardoning power under Article 72 on the advice of the Council of Ministers?
q.x: Maru Ram (1980) so held; Article 72 covers court-martial sentences and every death sentence.

q.s: Which of the following can the President pardon but a Governor cannot?
q.x: Only the President can pardon a death sentence; the Governor can suspend, remit or commute it.

q.s: Disqualification on the ground of defection is provided for in which Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: The Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985); conduct like campaigning for a rival party can amount to giving up membership.

q.s: Which of the following matters can NOT be settled by a Lok Adalat?
q.x: Lok Adalats settle compoundable and matrimonial matters but not divorce or non-compoundable offences.

q.s: Under which Article does a High Court have superintendence over all courts and tribunals in its territory?
q.x: Article 227 gives administrative and judicial superintendence; Article 226 is its writ power.

q.s: A High Court can issue writs for Fundamental Rights and 'for any other purpose' under:
q.x: Article 226 is wider than Article 32, which covers only Fundamental Rights.

q.s: Which of the following countries has a unitary form of government?
q.x: In the UK, Parliament holds all law-making power and local units are its creations.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: Single citizenship is a unitary feature.

q.s: The idea of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
q.x: Concurrent List - Australia; residuary powers with the Centre - Canada; single citizenship - UK.

q.s: Which of the following features is NOT correctly matched with its source?
o: Residuary powers with the Centre - Canada
Suspension of Fundamental Rights in emergency - Weimar Germany
q.x: Single citizenship was taken from the United Kingdom.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct is correct?
o: It has no statutory backing and is enforced by the ECI.
It is part of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
It is part of the Constitution.
It is enforced by the Supreme Court.
q.x: It is a consensus code of the parties; Part VII covers the party in power.

q.s: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force from:
o: The announcement of the election schedule
The issue of the election notification
q.x: Harbans Singh Jalal (1997) fixed the date of announcement.

q.s: Home voting in elections is available to voters above the age of:
q.x: Voters above 85 and persons with at least 40% benchmark disability can vote from home.

q.s: In ADR v. ECI (April 2024), the Supreme Court:
o: Ordered a 100% count of VVPAT slips
Ordered a return to paper ballots
Rejected a 100% count of VVPAT slips
q.x: The Court rejected full VVPAT counting and ordered symbol loading units to be sealed and kept 45 days.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, 2005, exemptions from disclosure are listed in:
q.x: Section 8 lists exemptions; the Second ARC wanted them read narrowly and linked RTI with whistle-blower protection.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Second ARC on the RTI Act?
o: Putting maximum information in the public domain
Proactive (suo motu) disclosure by public authorities
q.x: The Second ARC wanted the Section 8 exemptions read narrowly.

q.s: Which commission recommended 'localised emergency' and a fixed tenure for Governors?
q.x: Punchhi (2007-10) proposed these; Rajamannar sought State autonomy for Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in:
q.x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 and reported in 1988.

q.s: In the 2024 Odisha Assembly election, the BJP defeated which regional party?
q.x: The BJP ended the BJD's long rule in Odisha in 2024.

q.s: What is the BJP's role in the coalition government of Andhra Pradesh formed in 2024?
o: Supporting partner of a dominant regional party
Outside supporter not in the government
q.x: The TDP is dominant; the BJP and the Jana Sena are coalition partners.

q.s: Under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the number of Assembly seats in Andhra Pradesh is to rise from 175 to:
q.x: Sec. 26 (AP 175 to 225, Telangana 119 to 153) is subject to Art. 170 and the census after 2026.

q.s: Until the first census after 2026, Assembly constituencies are based on the Census of:
q.x: Delimitation based on 2001 Census figures continues; seat totals are frozen on the 1971 Census.

q.s: The election expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State is:
q.x: Rs 95 lakh in larger States and Rs 75 lakh in smaller States/UTs; Rs 40 lakh for Assembly candidates in larger States.

q.s: Election expenditure limits for candidates are prescribed under Rule 90 of the:
q.x: Rule 90 of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961; the ceiling applies to candidates, not parties.

q.s: Which committee (1998) recommended State funding of elections in India?
q.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee recommended partial State funding; it has not been adopted.

q.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's report was accepted in January 1958 by the:
q.x: The NDC accepted its three-tier scheme.

q.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1978) recommended:
q.x: Ashok Mehta proposed two tiers (Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat) with compulsory taxation powers.

q.s: The scheme of 'democratic decentralisation' recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee came to be known as:
q.x: Democratic decentralisation became Panchayati Raj, first launched at Nagaur (Rajasthan) in 1959.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The NDC insisted on a single rigid pattern for all States.
The NDC left the States free to evolve their own patterns of Panchayati Raj.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee held that Panchayati Raj needs no public co-operation.
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system.
q.x: Balwant Rai Mehta recommended three tiers and stressed public co-operation.

q.s: The State Finance Commission for Panchayats is constituted by the Governor under:
q.x: Art. 243I - State Finance Commission; Art. 280 - Finance Commission of India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the State Finance Commission is correct?
o: It is constituted by the President.
It advises the Union Finance Minister.
The Governor lays its report before the State Legislature.
q.x: It is set up by the Governor under Article 243I and advises the Governor.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a compulsory provision of the 73rd Amendment?
o: Minimum age of 21 years for membership
State Finance Commission every five years
Reservation of seats for backward classes
Direct elections at all three levels
q.x: Backward class reservation and devolution of the 29 subjects are voluntary, left to the States.

q.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
q.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects; the Twelfth lists 18 for municipalities.

q.s: The SHRESHTA scheme provides seats in private residential schools to meritorious students from:
q.x: SHRESHTA is for SC students; the Ambedkar Centres of Excellence also coach SC students.

q.s: Which department is the nodal department for urban local bodies in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: MA&UD is the nodal department; municipalities are governed by the AP Municipalities Act, 1965.

q.s: How many subjects are listed in the Twelfth Schedule for urban local bodies?
q.x: The 74th Amendment's Twelfth Schedule lists 18 subjects.

q.s: Reform of factor markets such as labour, land and power is classified as:
q.x: First-generation reforms covered trade, industry and exchange rates; factor-market, fiscal and governance reforms are second-generation.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Second-generation reforms include fiscal rules, disinvestment and governance reforms.
Second-generation reforms were confined to trade liberalisation.
Trade and exchange-rate reforms are second-generation reforms.
Factor-market reforms were part of the first-generation reforms.
q.x: First-generation reforms covered trade, industry and exchange rates.

q.s: Which of the following is issued by the Government of India and NOT by the RBI?
q.x: The RBI issues all notes except the Re 1 note; coins are also issued by the Government.

q.s: The RBI manages foreign exchange in India under the:
q.x: FEMA, 1999 replaced FERA, 1973.

q.s: Under the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loans scheme of Andhra Pradesh, crop loans are interest-free if repaid on time up to:
q.x: It is a State scheme for crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.

q.s: Under PMFBY, the farmer's premium for kharif food and oilseed crops is:
q.x: 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PMFBY is correct?
o: It has been voluntary for all farmers since Kharif 2020.
It has been compulsory for all loanee farmers since Kharif 2020.
Farmers pay 5% premium on kharif food crops.
It replaced the Kisan Credit Card scheme.
q.x: From Kharif 2020 PMFBY was made voluntary for all farmers, including loanees.

q.s: The Panchsheel principles were first set out in the 1954 India-China agreement on trade and intercourse with:
q.x: The agreement of 29 April 1954 on the Tibet region carried the five principles.

q.s: Panchsheel was incorporated in the Ten Principles of which conference?
q.x: The Bandung Afro-Asian Conference (1955) adopted ten principles including Panchsheel.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to promote international peace and security?
q.x: Article 51 (a DPSP) covers peace, just relations, respect for international law and arbitration.

q.s: Which of the following provision - subject pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Article 73 deals with the extent of the Union's executive power, including treaties.

q.s: Tank irrigation is most important in which of the following regions?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
q.x: Hard-rock, impervious terrain with poor groundwater makes tanks the main source in the southern peninsula.

q.s: What was the ad hoc sharing of Krishna water between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana after bifurcation?
q.x: The ad hoc split was 512 TMC for AP and 299 TMC for Telangana; Telangana seeks 50:50 on basin area.

q.s: Which body regulates the Krishna projects of AP and Telangana under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Section 85 created the KRMB (Hyderabad) and GRMB.

q.s: India amended its Patents Act in 2005 to introduce product patents in order to comply with the WTO's:
q.x: TRIPS required product patents in pharmaceuticals and food; GATS covers services.

q.s: Which of the following WTO agreements is NOT correctly matched with its subject?
o: SPS - Food safety and plant health
q.x: GATS covers trade in services; product patents came under TRIPS.

q.s: As per Census 2011, which was the only State to record negative decadal population growth (2001-11)?

q.s: Which of the following Census 2011 distinctions is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sikkim was the least populous State; Goa was the most urbanised.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the most literate district of India was:
q.x: Serchhip (Mizoram) had 98.76% literacy; Alirajpur (MP) the lowest, 37.22%.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the least literate district of India was:
q.x: Alirajpur in Madhya Pradesh had 37.22% literacy.

q.s: Which stage of the demographic transition model is marked by a population explosion?
q.x: In Stage II the birth rate stays high while the death rate falls, so growth is fastest.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the second stage of demographic transition?
q.x: In Stage II the birth rate stays high.

q.s: India's window of demographic dividend is expected to last up to about:
q.x: The window runs from 2005-06 to 2055-56, as the 15-64 working-age share is high.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: India's demographic window runs from about 2005-06 to 2055-56.
A demographic dividend arises from a high share of the elderly.
India's working-age group is defined as 25-50 years.
q.x: The dividend comes from a high share of the 15-64 working-age group.

q.s: As per Census 2011, what share of India's population was urban?
q.x: India was 31.1% urban in 2011; alternative measures (DEGURBA) suggest far higher hidden urbanisation.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Under-counting of urbanisation benefits peri-urban areas.
India is not over-urbanised at 31.1% urban, though its big cities lack infrastructure.
Census 2011 found India to be half urban.
q.x: Under-counting starves peri-urban areas of municipal funds.
